dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (JMA standard receipt software), compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. Program ORCR0640 handles inpatient diagnosis classification point aggregation.
evidence: fixed format, max line 78, no EXEC CICS/SQL
COPY count 46, CALL count 41 typical of ORCA subsystem

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance receipt (レセプト) processing system for inpatient (入院) claims; specifically diagnosis-category-based point aggregation (診療区分別点数集計) for NHI billing
purpose.summary: ORCR0640 is part of the JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt software system. It performs inpatient receipt processing, aggregating medical service points by diagnosis category for Japanese national health insurance claim forms. The program has an extensive revision history spanning 2002–2007 covering numerous regional public expense (地方公費) and insurance rule changes.

notable_features: Extensive Japanese-language comments (EUC-JP encoded, rendered as latin-1 mojibake)
46 COPY statements indicating heavy use of shared copybooks
41 CALL statements to other ORCA subprograms
699 PERFORM statements indicating complex procedural logic
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS (file-based, not DB2/CICS)
No COMP-3 usage despite financial calculations
Long revision history with versioned change log (01.00.01 through 03.05.01)
Fixed format with occasional lines over 72 chars (42 lines)
verdict.notes: File is 628KB / 13127 lines — a large production program. Japanese comments are EUC-JP encoded but decoded as latin-1, producing mojibake. The ORCA system is known to target GnuCOBOL (formerly OpenCOBOL) on Linux. No COMP-3 is unusual for financial code but consistent with ORCA's coding style. Source truncated to first 16000 chars; full procedure division not visible but mechanical indicators confirm all four divisions present.
